key_insight: pUniFind is a single large-scale deep model trained on >100 million spectra that unifies peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing, substantially improving peptide identification and discovery of modifications.
problem_solved: Overcomes limited accuracy and fragmentation ambiguity in peptide identification and open modification discovery by combining scoring and de novo prediction in one multimodal model trained at massive scale.
method: Unified architecture that performs both peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing within one model.
Multimodal training on spectrum signals, peptide sequences and metadata (including modifications) to learn joint representations.
Scale: trained on 100M+ spectra to improve generalization and enable reliable identification of modified peptides and novel variants.
impact: Shows that large, task‑unified multimodal models can raise identification sensitivity and modification discovery in proteomics, encouraging AI practitioners to apply large-scale multimodal training for domain-specific sequence+signal tasks.
visual_elements: Simplified model architecture diagram showing spectrum encoder + sequence decoder and dual outputs (score + de novo sequence).
Bar/line chart comparing identification rates and modification discovery vs prior methods (before/after).
Data-source infographic showing multimodal training inputs: raw spectra, peptide labels, PTM annotations (with counts, e.g., 100M+ spectra).
Workflow diagram: raw spectrum → pUniFind → (a) peptide score for database search, (b) open de novo sequence & modification candidate
paper_title: A large-scale unified deep learning model for peptide mass spectrum interpretation trained on multimodal data
paper_authors: Jiale Zhao, Pengzhi Mao, Kaifei Wang, Yiming Li, Yaping Peng
